A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same NeuroAda paper. Their main text, equations, Figures 1-7, Tables 1-7, and Appendices A-E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning results on commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, and GLUE, plus memory, throughput, and parameter-selection experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds two higher-budget NeuroAda result rows to the arithmetic evaluation.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain the same magnitude-based top-k selection, zero-initialized sparse deltas, frozen backbone, and post-training weight merging. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: The commonsense, arithmetic, and GLUE datasets and task requirements remain unchanged. The additional Table 3 rows reuse existing arithmetic tasks. Appendix A.1's new mention of multimodal learning does not introduce a multimodal experiment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2-4 and the mask-based/full-tuning comparisons is unchanged. Table 3 adds only NeuroAda rows, without matching higher-budget arithmetic baseline rows for LLaMA2-7B or LLaMA3-8B.

E3.justification: Table 5 changes the designated best top-20 warmup ratio for LLaMA-7B on GSM8K from 0.10 to 0.00, while retaining the search candidates. This revises a reported experimental setting; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. Other stated evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4 and Figures 4-7 retain the same mask-based comparison, memory/throughput study, neuron-participation analysis, and four parameter-selection strategies. The new Table 3 entries extend ordinary benchmark reporting.

E5.justification: Tables 2-3 retain averages over three runs with different seeds, and Table 4 retains means and standard deviations over five runs. Appendix C.1's seed-selection and replacement information is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 corrects higher-budget LLaMA-7B/13B averages from 68.4 to 65.7 and 71.4 to 68.4, with their component scores unchanged. Section 5.2 correspondingly reduces the stated LLaMA-13B advantage over LoRA from 6% to 3%. Two new six-task rows report LLaMA2-7B at 0.404% trainable parameters, averaging 66.8, and LLaMA3-8B at 0.343%, averaging 70.7. These are limited corrections and additions within the existing arithmetic evaluation.

T1.justification: Equations 1-6, the top-k definition, sparse-update formulation, and memory-scaling derivations retain the same mathematical content. No new assumptions, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about neuron-level adaptation, state-of-the-art performance with at most 0.02% trainable parameters, and memory savings up to 60%. The local arithmetic-margin correction does not redefine those core claims.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning neuron coverage, magnitude selection, and memory efficiency remain unchanged. Section 7 still limits evaluation to models up to 13B and identifies larger models and vision-language tasks as future work; removing its citation does not change these boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix C's Table 5 revises the reproducibility information by identifying 0.00 rather than 0.10 as the selected top-20 warmup ratio. Other implementation details, hyperparameter grids, hardware disclosures, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Dong et al. (2025a) citation from the future vision-language discussion and adds explicit citations to already-discussed Zhang et al. (2024b,a) in Appendix D's sparse-training comparison. The bibliography and main related-work discussion remain unchanged. Newly inserted appendix citation strings also contain unresolved question marks.

P1.justification: Prose changes are localized: Appendix A.1 adds a sentence connecting commonsense reasoning to multimodal learning, Appendix D adds a comparative phrase, and Section 5.2 corrects a numerical statement. The narrative and section hierarchy remain intact, while new unresolved citation markers reduce polish.

P2.justification: Tables 2-3 add blue highlighting to higher-budget NeuroAda averages, and Table 3 expands by two rows. Surrounding text and the beginning of the conclusion reflow across pages 7-9. Figures 1-7 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects two arithmetic averages to agree with their unchanged task scores and reduces the overstated LLaMA-13B margin over LoRA from six to three percentage points. The additional arithmetic rows also improve reporting completeness. These provide a modest net improvement in empirical accuracy, despite new unresolved appendix citations and the unexplained revision to the selected warmup setting.
